messages:
sophia: Heads-up — planning changes to customer-facing audit events and archive posture. Need alignment on log signing (WORM), KMS key rotation model, and schema additions for exportable proofs. Any hard constraints from infra/legal before I write the RFC?

raj: Which customer groups are we targeting here? enterprise SOC2 customers, gov customers, e-discovery? different needs.

melissa: Primary ask is enterprise SOC2 + some regulated customers who require verifiable immutability and provenance for legal requests. A few customers may ask for a signed manifest they can hold.

carlos: Practically: we can put objects in S3 with Object Lock (compliance mode) and use KMS CMKs. But key custody is the trick — for Private deployments customers may want customer-managed CMKs in their account/HSM. Cross-account indexes and signature verification need stable key identifiers/aliases.

sophia: My draft idea: keep a single canonical audit blob per retention window (e.g., daily/rolling hour), generate a per-tenant signing key (as an envelope key encrypted by a tenant-scoped CMK), produce a signed manifest with a compact Merkle root for the events, store the manifest alongside the blob (and in the system index). Exports = {blob, manifest, cert}. Does that sound feasible?

raj: Sounds reasonable. A few notes on RBAC: only a small set of principals should be able to create/rotate signing keys. Propose new roles: `audit-signer`, `audit-admin`. Key rotation events must themselves be auditable (signed and emitted). Also need migration plan for existing logs if schema changes.

melissa: From contracts/compliance: we need explicit fields in the event schema to make exported evidence machine-readable. Suggest fields like `evidence_requested: boolean`, `chain_of_custody_id: string`, `exported_by: string`, and `proof_method: string` (e.g., `KMS-signed`, `HSM-signed`, `none`).

carlos: Example minimal manifest we could produce (pseudo):

```
{
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "period_start": "2026-01-20T00:00:00Z",
  "period_end": "2026-01-20T01:00:00Z",
  "blob_s3_key": "audit/t-123/2026-01-20/00-01.parquet",
  "merkle_root": "3f5a...",
  "signature": "BASE64(...)",
  "signer_key_alias": "alias/audit-signer/t-123",
  "proof_method": "KMS-envelope",
  "schema_version": "audit-v2",
  "events_count": 12456
}
```

carlos: Implementation note: KMS CMK rotation does not re-encrypt existing encrypted data automatically unless we copy objects. So if customers require that archived objects are encrypted under a new CMK version for each rotation, we need a rewrap/copy pipeline. More common pattern is to keep the object data key wrapped with the CMK alias and keep an immutable signature that references the key alias + rotation history.

raj: Important: signing key lifecycle must include backup/escrow procedures (legal holds!). Also define what happens on key compromise: Do we produce revocation manifests and re-sign new manifests? Need playbook.

melissa: For legal holds we must support preservation beyond normal retention. Contracts should allow us to surface a signed manifest proving an event existed at a time. I will draft contract language that relies on `signature` + `merkle_root` + `schema_version`.

ops-bot: <link> Compliance playbook: https://redwood.internal/policy/log-retention-playbook (access controlled) :page_facing_up: 

sophia: Quick question re: customer-facing export format — should we give customers the raw signed manifest + raw blobs, or provide a verifier tool (recommended) so they can validate signatures against a published signing certificate?

carlos: Provide both. Raw artifacts for audits, plus a small `verify-audit-export` CLI that consumes manifest + blob and validates the signature chain. For customer-managed CMKs we publish the verification path (public cert or JWK).

raj: RFC checklist I will require: RBAC changes (roles + least privilege), key lifecycle (create/rotate/revoke/escrow), export format + verifier, migration plan for existing logs, retention & hold semantics, and monitoring/alerts for signing failures.

melissa: Also include SLA/notice language for key compromise and subpoenas. We need clear timelines and responsibilities.

sophia: Action items: 1) raj to open RFC with checklist; 2) carlos to prototype signing/manifest flow (P0: proof-of-concept Merkle root + KMS envelope); 3) melissa to draft contract/compliance language and preservation clauses; 4) I'll mock schema changes and sample export flows.

raj: ACK. I'll start RFC and link back here.

carlos: I'll spin up a small prototype this week and post logs. Expect a short demo.

melissa: I'll post first draft legal language by EOD Fri.

sophia: Thanks all — will use these notes for the RFC. :thumbsup:
